title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: Applying the Contract Discount to the Uplifted Rate
content:
## Clause

In the Dangerous Goods Acceptance loading surcharge, the contract discount operates on the uplifted surcharge per container — the figure that already includes the total uplift — and on nothing else; it never touches the base amount on its own. The surcharge per container after discount is the uplifted surcharge per container multiplied by one hundred less the discount percentage, and divided by one hundred. With a discount of 0 the uplifted figure passes through unchanged. Nothing is rounded at this point: the figure is kept to the ten-thousandth of a dollar.

## Worked example (invented figures)

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Base per container | 300.00 |
| Total uplift | 55 percent |
| Uplifted surcharge per container | 465.00 |
| Discount | 12 percent |
| Per container after discount | 465.00 multiplied by 88, divided by 100, giving 409.20 |

## A second illustration (invented figures)

Uplifted surcharge per container 244.375 and a discount of 10 percent: 244.375 multiplied by 90 and divided by 100 gives 219.9375, which is kept exactly as it stands.
